# Instructions for AI coding agents

This is an **oxframe** project: procedural animation in Rust. Scenes are
`async fn`s; every `.await` on an animation takes time.

This project uses **oxframe {{SDK_VERSION}}**. Use the docs of exactly this
version — the API changes between versions:

- Guide: https://oxframe.dev/docs/{{DOCS_SERIES}}
- Docs for models: https://oxframe.dev/docs/{{DOCS_SERIES}}/llms.txt and https://oxframe.dev/docs/{{DOCS_SERIES}}/llms-full.txt
- API reference: https://docs.rs/oxframe/{{SDK_VERSION}}/oxframe/

## Layout

- `src/main.rs` — scenes (`#[oxframe::scene] async fn name(view: View)`) and `main()` with `Project::new(..).scene(..).main()`.
- `src/<scene>.meta.json` — markers, eases, tunables and transition length edited in the editor. **Do not hand-edit unless asked; never delete keys.**
- `oxframe.toml` — settings for the `oxframe` CLI. `assets/` — images, audio.

## Commands (run from the project root)

| Goal | Command |
|---|---|
| **Check a change** (compile, then look) | `oxframe check` → `out/check/storyboard.png` and `out/check/report.json`. Exit 1 if any issue is an error. |
| Scene tree at one time | `oxframe inspect --at 2.5` (JSON: kind, name, bounds, text, `file:line`; `transition` with kind and progress while one is playing). `--graph` adds `passes`: vector, then composite |
| One full-size still | `oxframe snapshot --at 1.5` → prints the PNG path |
| Scene length, markers | `cargo run -q -- info` (JSON) |
| Final video | `oxframe render` → `out/<project>.mp4` (needs ffmpeg) |

Add `--json` to any command for one JSON object on stdout (`ok`, `exit`, and
on a compile error `diagnostics` plus `hints`). `oxframe mcp` is an MCP server
on stdio with tools `check`, `storyboard`, `render_frame`, `inspect`,
`list_components`, `docs_search` and `render`.

`oxframe dev` is an interactive editor server for humans; do not run it in an
agent session (it never exits).

## Model in five lines

1. `let s = view.add(Rect::new().size(200.0).x(-300.0).fill(color!("#e13238")));` — builder sets the start; `add` returns a `Copy` handle.
2. `s.x().to(300.0, 1.0).await;` — animate a property (target, seconds) and wait.
3. `all((a, b, c)).await` — run together (a tuple, or `all(items.iter().map(|x| x.fade_in()))`); `stagger(0.1, &items, |x| x.pop_in()).await` — one after another; `wait_for(secs)`; `spawn(fut)` for background. Never `Box::pin` or `BoxFuture`.
4. Properties are `Signal<T>`: `.get()`, `.set(v)`, `.to(v, secs).ease(e)`, `.bind(move || ..)`.
5. Coordinates: origin at the center, y down, default canvas 1920×1080 at 60 fps; rotation in degrees. Prefer theme tokens (`Accent`, `.display()`, `.padding(Md)`, `Normal`) over hardcoded colors and sizes. Place with `.next_to(other, Side::Bottom)`, `.align_to(other, Edge::Top)`, `.to_edge(Edge::Top)`, `.center_in(other)` and `.width(pct(80))` instead of pixel guesses. `Project::aspects([Landscape, Portrait, Square])` and `view.is_portrait()` cover 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1. `Project::theme(...)` or `[theme]` in `oxframe.toml` restyles the whole video.

## Transitions

`transition(Transition::slide(Dir::Left)).await` at the start of a scene (not the first) blends the previous scene's last frame over this one for the theme's normal duration. Also `fade`, `wipe(Dir::…)`, `zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, `.duration(0.6)`, `.ease(...)`, `.overlap()`, and `Transition::custom(|t| Blend { ... })`. Nodes added before the call are visible during the blend.

## Camera

For a big diagram or a close look at a detail: build it inside
`view.add(Camera::new())`, then `cam.fit(node, padding, secs)`,
`cam.center_on(node, secs)`, `cam.zoom().to(2.0, secs)`, `cam.reset(secs)`.
Titles added to `view` stay on screen.

## Components

Prefer these over drawing the block yourself. Each has `enter()`, `next()` and `exit()`.

- `TitleCard::new("Binary search").subtitle("O(log n)")` — title, then the subtitle on `next`.
- `ChapterMarker::new("1  Search")` — label on the top safe edge.
- `BulletList::new(["Take the middle", "Compare", "Drop half"])` — `next` reveals one row.
- `CodeExplainer::new("lo + (hi - lo) / 2").step(1, 1, "the middle")` — `next` focuses that line range.
- `FlowDiagram::new().edge("Client", "API").edge("API", "DB")` — laid out in layers; `.down()` stacks them. `next` highlights the next node.
- `Callout::new(node).text("the middle")` — arrow and caption above `node`.
- `LowerThird::new("Ada").role("walks the half")` — name plate on the bottom safe edge.
- `EndCard::new("That's the search").note("Repeat from the top")` — closing card.

See `.claude/skills/oxframe/reference.md` for the full API cheat sheet.

## Voice

`voice("one two").start()` speaks now. `line.at_word("two").await` waits for that word; `line.await` waits until the end. Await the line, or `oxframe check` errors because it runs past the scene. A line is `.priority()`, so it ducks a soundtrack built with `.duck_under_voice()`. Pass a `TtsProvider` with `Project::tts`. Without one, the length is estimated. A real recording is cached under `tts/`; commit that folder so CI renders it without an API key. `oxframe render --subtitles out.srt` writes the lines (`.vtt` by extension).

## Rules

- **Deterministic**: never use `std::time`, `Instant`, `rand::thread_rng` or other entropy; use `random()` / `random_range(a, b)` (seeded by `Project::seed`). Avoid iterating `HashMap` to decide what to draw; use `Vec`/`BTreeMap`.
- Names for `wait_until`, `tune!`, `ease!` are `[a-z0-9_-]+` (checked at compile time for the macros).
- Colors: `color!("#rrggbb")` (compile-time checked) or `Color::rgb(r, g, b)` with 0..1 floats.
- Keep each scene a straight story: prefer `all(..)`/`stagger(..)` and the helpers `fade_in()`, `fade_out()`, `pop_in()`, `slide_in(Side::Left)`, `draw_on()` (timed by the theme; `.duration(s)` to change) over manual tweens and frame loops; `next_frame()` only for per-frame logic.
- After each visual change run `oxframe check`, open `out/check/storyboard.png` and read `report.json`, fix what it reports, and run it again. Do not report success while it exits non-zero.
- Name nodes that matter in the story: `.name("title")`. Without a name, check and inspect label the node by the `add` call site (`src/main.rs:42`).

## Common compile errors

- *"closure may outlive the current function"* in `bind`: clone the signals first and use `move`:
  `let (ax, bx) = (a.x(), b.x()); label.x().bind(move || (ax.get() + bx.get()) / 2.0);`
- *"`()` is not an animation"*: a closure ending in `;` returns nothing. Drop the `;` (`|r| r.fade_in()`), or return `async move { a.await; b.await; }` for several steps.
- `Signal::new(0.0)` ambiguous float: write `0.0f64`.
- `all` of a few different animations takes a **tuple** — note the double parentheses: `all((a, b))`.
